config.borderlesswindow.title: Borderless Window Settings
borderlesswindow.options.screen_mode.too: Choose between a normal window, borderless fullscreen, or Minecraft's regular exclusive fullscreen.
borderlesswindow.options.f11_mode.name: F11 Mode
borderlesswindow.options.f11_mode.toolti: What the F11 key does: toggle borderless fullscreen, toggle Minecraft's regular exclusive fullscreen, or cycle through all three screen modes.
borderlesswindow.options.fps_overlay_mod: Shows an FPS counter on screen. Simple displays only the current FPS; Extended shows a single line with the current FPS plus the Min, Avg and Max FPS over the last 15 seconds. The overlay hides itself while the debug screen (F3) is open or the GUI is hidden (F1).
borderlesswindow.options.fps_overlay_pos: Corner of the screen where the FPS overlay is drawn.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_terrain.too: The atmospheric haze that fades out distant terrain, including the Nether's thick fog. Turn Off for a clearer view into the distance. Fog from the Blindness and Darkness effects is never affected by these toggles.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_water.name: Water Fog
borderlesswindow.options.fog_water.toolt: The fog seen while underwater. Turn Off to see much farther when diving.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_lava.name: Lava Fog
borderlesswindow.options.fog_lava.toolti: The fog seen while submerged in lava. Turn Off to see through lava while inside it.
borderlesswindow.options.fog_powder_snow: The fog seen while inside powder snow. Turn Off to keep your view clear.
borderlesswindow.options.cloud_height.to: Raises or lowers the cloud layer, between y=64 and y=320. "Default" leaves each dimension's own height untouched, and "(Regular)" marks Minecraft's own, which is 192. Dimensions with no clouds at all — the Nether, the End, cloudless dimensions from other mods — stay that way at any setting: this moves clouds, it never adds them.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_water.t: The rippling texture drawn over your view while underwater. Turn Off for a clear view while swimming. This is separate from Water Fog, which controls how far you can see rather than what is drawn on the screen.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_fire.to: The flames drawn across your view while you are burning. Turn Off to keep your view clear while on fire. The suffocation overlay shown when your head is inside a solid block is never affected.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_fire_sm: Keeps the fire overlay, but hides it while you have Fire Resistance. Minecraft draws that same overlay while you swim in lava, so this also clears your view inside lava for as long as the effect lasts. Requires the Fire Overlay to be On.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_pumpkin: The blur drawn around your view while wearing a carved pumpkin. Turn Off to see normally, so a pumpkin can be worn against endermen without the visual cost. Helmet overlays added by other mods are never affected.
The frost border drawn around your view while freezing in powder snow. Turn Off to keep your view clear. Note this border is also a warning that you are taking freeze damage; the frozen hearts on the HUD still show it.
The purple warp drawn over your view while standing inside a Nether portal. Turn Off to see clearly while building or aligning portals.
borderlesswindow.options.overlay_spyglas: The scope texture and the black bars drawn while looking through a spyglass. Turn Off to keep the zoom across the whole screen. The zoom itself is unchanged; only the frame around it is removed.
borderlesswindow.options.camera_bob.name: Camera Bobbing
borderlesswindow.options.camera_bob.tool: How much the camera sways as you walk. Full is vanilla. Vertical Only keeps the up-and-down bounce but removes the side-to-side sway and the tilt, so the horizon stays level -- the tilt is what most people find nauseating. Off holds the camera still. Requires Minecraft's own View Bobbing option to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.hand_bob.name: Hand Bobbing
borderlesswindow.options.hand_bob.toolti: Whether the held item sways as you walk, controlled separately from the camera. Turn Off for a steady hand while keeping camera movement, or leave On with the camera off. Requires Minecraft's own View Bobbing option to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_fov.too: Minecraft's own FOV Effects slider, which scales all four options below at once. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so this brings it back here. It is the same setting as the one in Accessibility Settings and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_speed.name: Speed FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_speed.toolt: How much the view widens as you move faster -- sprinting, Speed potions, anything that raises movement speed. 100% is vanilla. Minecraft has one slider for all four of these together; here they are separate. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_flying.name: Flying FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_flying.tool: The extra widening while flying in creative. Elytra gliding is not affected -- that is not the same flying. It is a small 10%% pull, and sprint speed usually masks it. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_bow.name: Bow FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_bow.tooltip: The zoom that builds up while you draw a bow. 100% is vanilla, 0% holds the view still. The spyglass is never affected: its zoom is what the item does, not a visual effect. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.fov_fluid.name: Fluid FOV
borderlesswindow.options.fov_fluid.toolt: The squeeze applied while your head is in water or lava. 100% is vanilla. Requires Minecraft's own FOV Effects to be on.
borderlesswindow.options.vanilla_distort: Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider, which scales both options below at once. Sodium's video settings leave it out, so this brings it back here. It is the same setting as the one in Accessibility Settings and is saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's. Lowering it also brings back the green nausea texture, which is Minecraft's replacement cue.
borderlesswindow.options.distortion_port: How much the view warps while you stand in a Nether portal. 100% is vanilla. Minecraft has one slider for this and for Nausea together; here they are separate. Sits under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider: with that at Off, nothing warps and this has no effect.
borderlesswindow.options.distortion_naus: How much the view warps while you have the Nausea effect, from a potion, a pufferfish or suspicious stew. 100% is vanilla. Sits under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider: with that at Off, nothing warps and this has no effect.
borderlesswindow.options.enchantment_lev: How enchantment levels are written next to the enchantment name. Minecraft only has Roman numerals up to X and shows raw text like "enchantment.level.11" above that. Mixed keeps the Roman numerals and switches to plain numbers past X; the other two use a single style at every level. Levels go up to 255.
